born.why: The code improves upon the original by using trait-based inference to guess safety when direct experience is missing, prioritizing 'eat' for known-safe fruits to maximize energy gain, and using a risk threshold based on shared characteristics with poisonous fruits to avoid learning costly lessons.

The code prioritizes starvation survival, exploits known safe species by eating them, avoids known poisons and their trait-proxies (color/smell), and uses "taste" for novel fruits to safely gather data with minimal hunger cost.

The code adds a "hunger threshold" for tasting unknown fruits to avoid pointless risks when satiated, and prioritizes eating known safe fruits only when genuinely hungry, preventing overeating or unnecessary handling of low-value items while retaining the critical poison-avoidance logic.

The code prioritizes survival by rejecting known poisons and trait-matched hazards, eats known safe fruits immediately for efficiency, and only tastes new fruits when hunger is sufficiently high to justify the risk, preventing unnecessary harm when satiated.

The code prioritizes efficiency by eating known-safe fruits immediately, uses trait-based inference (color/smell) to avoid similar poisonous species without needing direct experience, and defaults to 'taste' for discovery to minimize starvation risk while learning.

It distinguishes between known-poisonous, unknown, and proven-safe fruits by using the diary to calculate an average harm score, ensuring she tastes unknown items cautiously and only eats those with a history of low or negative harm (benefit).
